findings.title: CHAINALYSIS BREACH SPILLS CREDENTIALS AND LIVE TOKENS FOR EVERY CUSTOMER
findings.comment: The firm what hunts crooks on the blockchain got boarded by an on-path attack leakin' password hashes and live tokens for the whole crew — law enforcement logins now floatin' where the markets can smell 'em.

findings.title: SSHHOLE: OPENSSH ROOT LOGIN VIA ONE LONG PASSWORD
findings.comment: Musl-based ships (Alpine, OpenWrt, Yocto) accepted any 256+ char password as root nine hours after disclosure; patched in OpenSSH 10.6p2, but restart sshd or the old binary keeps poarin' the grog.

findings.title: ECAPTURE V2.10.0 SETS SAIL
findings.comment: The eBPF TLS-tap now reads GnuTLS 3.8.10-3.8.13 layouts an' verifies QUIC v1/v2 in its pcapng plunder; handy for spyin' on yer own C2 noise too.

findings.title: FIVE AGENCIES ORDER COLD CHAIN CONTROLLERS OFF THE INTERNET
findings.comment: CISA, FBI an' shipmates warn villains can force freezers into endless defrost cycles an' spoil the cargo; segment the OT VLAN an' change default passwords, ye walruses.

findings.title: HYPERLOADER RUNS SHELLCODE IN A HIDDEN GUEST VM
findings.comment: New WHVP toy runs Stardust shellcode on its own guest vCPU so userland EDR hooks see naught; kernel callbacks still watch the horizon, so tune those detections.

findings.title: FRANCE BLAMES IRGC SHAHID KAVEH FOR FRIDGE ATTACKS
findings.comment: France formally named the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh cyber unit for cooking supermarket freezers to 50C, summoned Iran's envoy and seeks arrest warrants — statecraft served with spoiled fish.

findings.title: MICROSOFT: STORM-3358 WIELDS ARTEX AI FRAMEWORK
findings.comment: Cambodia-based Storm-3358 lets an agentic AI pentest framework do the plunderin' — recon, exploitation and RAT droppin' at machine speed while the crew naps in Phnom Penh.

findings.title: CERT-IN FLAGS CRAFTY FALCON AI RAID ON FINTECHS
findings.comment: India's CERT-In says this AI-assisted crew strikes fintechs on weekends, tests with one-rupee transfers, then drains wallets — the weekend watchman's worst nightmare, matey.

findings.title: ESET NAMES SLIPPYNUNCHUCKS, HIJACKS SOGOU KEYBOARD
findings.comment: A China-aligned crew hijacked the Sogou keyboard's plaintext update path to side-load DarkVigil on Chinese-speaking targets across Asia — yer typing tutor turned informer.

findings.title: SEKOIA TIES POISONED SOURCE CAMPAIGN TO APT29
findings.comment: SVR's finest poisoned a Ukrainian analytics script on thousands of sites to serve patched mobile exploits with zero clicks — old CVEs, new tricks, and nobody aboard noticed a thing.

findings.title: BITTER APT DEPLOYS NEW PAPRAT BACKDOOR
findings.comment: Bitter delivers a fresh C++ and Rust RAT via fake diplomatic documents and VHDX images at South Asian governments and energy firms — phishing with an official seal, how dignified.

findings.title: OPENSSH BYPASS ACTIVELY EXPLOITED
findings.comment: Oversized passwords now unlock vulnerable musl-based OpenSSH accounts; root fell within hours, because apparently “reject login” was merely nautical décor.

findings.title: BARRACUDA FLAWS CHAIN TO ROOT
findings.comment: CVE-2026-116606 chains with CVE-2026-111560 for unauthenticated root on ESG appliances—an email gateway that thoughtfully forwards attackers to the helm.

findings.title: RANSOMWARE ABUSES HYPERVISOR ADMIN PATHS
findings.comment: Raiders reused PRTG-held ESXi root passwords, disabled execInstalledOnly and encrypted hosts; Proxmox fell through plaintext notes and VNC, no fancy escape required.

findings.title: AGENTIC TOOLING AUTOMATES CYBERCRIME
findings.comment: ARTEX fleets now scan, exploit and pursue financial targets at machine speed; even mediocre corsairs can command tireless raiding parties from one prompt.
